verdict.rationale: Gmail documents standard IMAP/POP/SMTP support for non-Gmail clients and a full Gmail API for programmatic access, letting users connect other clients like Outlook/Thunderbird — supporting openness in principle. However, community hands-on evidence concretely contradicts full IMAP fidelity: IDLE doesn't sync read-status changes, and a developer who spent a year building a desktop client via IMAP found it 'completely unsuited' to Gmail's paradigm, forcing reliance on Google's proprietary API instead. Missing for 10: JMAP support (not mentioned anywhere), evidence of complete data export fidelity (labels/threads) via open protocols, and resolution of the documented IMAP sync limitations.
